_doc: HAND-AUTHORED for T-0497. The Dalton Data Bank's Illinois census index, 1840 block, read entry by entry off daltondatabank.net/Illinois.html on 2026-09-05. NAMES ONLY: the page itself is not committed (its rights are check_required; a name index of a public-domain census is fact, the page is theirs).
the_ladder: An 1840 index row is LATER EVIDENCE twice over — later than 1835, and mediated by somebody else's index rather than read off the sheet. Under the ratified ladder, 1839/1840 alone is never an 1835 residence. Nothing here mints, grades or regrades a resident; T-0513 consolidates and T-0514/T-0515 apply.
what_this_index_actually_is: The ticket that asked for this reading described a 'free 1840 Chicago head-of-household index by ward' and called it 'the cheapest second reading of the 1840 heads the project can get'. That is WRONG, and the reading is what shows it: the Dalton Data Bank is a ONE-SURNAME genealogical databank. Its Illinois page indexes Dalton, Dolton and Daulton entries and nothing else — 'There are over 5000 surname entries in this file' — so its 1840 census block is 20 Illinois rows, of which 3 stand in a Chicago ward. It is not a city name list, it cannot be a second reading of the 964 IPUMS households, and it cannot cross-check the spelling of any 1840 head who was not called Dalton.

wards.as_the_index_gives_them: Ward numbers only — '1st Ward', '1 Ward', '2 Ward' — written into the place string beside the county. No boundary, street or extent is stated anywhere on the page.
wards.town_finding: None. Ticket rule 5 asked for the ward boundaries this index implies; it implies none. What it does carry is that Chicago was divided into at least two numbered wards by the 1840 enumeration, which this project already holds from the 1837 charter and which is five years after the scene date either way.

what_it_does_not_supply: household composition — no age bands, no counts, no line
the printed page and line of the census sheet the row came from
any 1835 residence, and any bridge from 1840 back to 1835
any head of household not named Dalton, Dolton or Daulton

negatives.query: a per-ward page, or any page of the site holding non-Dalton Chicago heads
negatives.result: none exists. The site's only Illinois pages are Illinois.html and Illinois_Page_2.html (plus Newspapers/IllinoisNewspapers.htm); the ward is a value inside a row, not a page. The ticket's 'fetch every 1840 Chicago ward page' therefore has exactly two pages to fetch, and both were.

negatives.query: the Dalton surname across data/census/1840/household_heads.csv.gz — PR #670's 210 named heads
negatives.result: 0 hits. The three Chicago-ward Dalton households this index names are NOT on the seven printed pages (229–235) read so far, so they lie on unread images of the deposit — a specific thing for T-0496 and T-0657–T-0659 to watch for.

negatives.query: the Dalton surname across data/research/civic/records/ — the 1833–1835 poll and voter lists
negatives.result: 0 hits. No Dalton voted or was polled in the town this project reconstructs.

negatives.query: the Dalton surname across data/research/land_sales/records/ — the federal tract sales through 1836
negatives.result: 0 hits, against two Cook County purchases the databank's own land-sales section prints for a George Dalton on 25 and 27 June 1836. Neither register contradicts the other: the committed sweep covers seven townships around the town (T38N–T41N, R13E–R15E) and Cook County is far larger. Recorded, not resolved — see dalton_index_land_sales_note.
1 household — hh_dalton_edward, the letter-list Edward Dalton, already carrying this index as an unasserted candidate (T-0479). No other Dalton is in the town.

dalton_index_land_sales_note: Illinois_Page_2.html's ILLINOIS LAND SALES section, sourced to the Illinois Archives, prints under COOK COUNTY: 'George Dalton, price $1055, 6/25/1836; same date three other purchases at $687.50 and $343.75.' and 'George Dalton, price $875, 6/27/1836'. RESOLVED by T-0830, and it was not what this note supposed. All five are in the Archives' register (purchase nos 0363249, 0363250, 0379985, 0515062, 0515063), at exactly those prices, as canal sales of June 1836 — and the land_sales sweep does not hold them because the register gives them NO section: the tract is a lot and block in a platted town, and a by-section query can never return a row with no section. The supposition here — 'this is a purchase outside the seven townships, a lead and not a fault' — was wrong. A whole-county list walk (land_sales/coverage.json § completeness_probe) finds 619 such rows dated through 1836, 466 of them in 1836. Reading them is T-1028. Nothing about this touches the 1840 census reading, and George Dalton's residence reads UNKNOWN on all five rows: a purchase is a transaction, never a home.
